## Bottleneck breakdown

Phase timing as share of total (from per-phase instrumentation in the C binary).

| Device | Model | FFN | GDN q/k/v proj | GDN out proj | Full attn | GDN conv | GDN decay | GDN scan |
|--------|-------|-----|----------------|--------------|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|
| rk3588-t3_08b | Qwen3.5-0.8B | 54.1% | 29.9% | 8.2% | 7.5% | 0.3% | 0.0% | 0.0% |
| jetson-j1_08b | Qwen3.5-0.8B | 55.9% | 24.5% | 10.5% | 8.3% | 0.7% | 0.1% | 0.1% |
| rk3588-t3 | Qwen3.5-4B | 72.4% | 13.8% | 8.1% | 5.6% | 0.1% | 0.0% | 0.0% |
| jetson-j1 | Qwen3.5-4B | 69.9% | 15.0% | 7.9% | 7.1% | 0.1% | 0.0% | 0.0% |
| rk3588-t4 | Qwen3.5-4B | — | — | — | — | — | — | — |

**Key findings:**
- **FFN dominates** (54–72% across all device/model combos) — the model is
  matmul-bound, not recurrence-bound. GDN's novel kernels (Conv1D, decay, scan)
  are <1% of total time.
- **GEMV optimization matters more than core class:** RK3588-A76 with the
  row-sweep GEMV (`2e752af`) achieves 1.04 tok/s on 4B, vs 0.09 tok/s at the
  pre-optimization commit `def3f29` — an 11.6× gain from software alone.
- **0.8B is practical on low-end edge:** the A57 achieves 2.7 tok/s on 0.8B,
  making it deployable for real-time assistance on passively-cooled hardware.

## Cross-device scaling (matched GEMV code)

| Metric | Cortex-A57 (Jetson) | Cortex-A76 (RK3588) | A76/A57 |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------|---------|
| 0.8B tok/s | 2.70 | 7.98 | 3.0× |
| 4B tok/s | 0.43 | 1.04 | 2.4× |
| 0.8B TTFT (s) | ~0.37 | ~0.125 | 3.0× |
| 4B TTFT (s) | ~2.3 | ~0.96 | 2.4× |

The A76 is 2.4–3.0× faster than the A57, consistent with the ~1.6× clock
advantage (2.4 vs 1.48 GHz) plus the A76's wider pipeline (2× FMA/cycle
vs A57's 1×). The 4B ratio is smaller because the larger working set pushes
both cores closer to DRAM bandwidth limits.

> t4 (pre-GEMV baseline) excluded from this comparison. A76 4B = t3 only.

## Methodology

- Binary: `bench_gdn_e2e_decode[_08b]_<isa>` — full Qwen3.5 forward pass in C
  with NEON GEMV (row-sweep, OpenMP parallel tiles) for the projection matmuls.
- Protocol: governor=performance, 3+ independent runs, pre/post thermal
  snapshots. All manifests confirm `dirty=false`.
- Weights: random fp32 (benchmark only — no model loading).
- Replicates: see the Spread column. On this fleet, single-run variance can
  reach 1.68× (bead ob-bf7). All entries here show <1.15× spread.
